title: The accepted value has no durable home and no owner publishes a write for it
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T3.3); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (document control change note, A2.4.3.2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-004 Data table)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 9 and 10; s8 BR4, BR5, BR10; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13; CON s11
description: The acceptance fixes a band and must be recorded with its rule version, and no source says where the accepted value, the acceptance marker accepted_at and the accepting user are persisted after the split. The ownership rows of the context pack give S1 no table at all, so the service schema can hold only the library objects of DP-03 and the idempotency key. TSD S1 T3.1 declares valuation as a NEW Workbench table with accepted, stale_flag and age_days (DF-COL-027, DF-COL-043, DF-COL-044), and the FSD of v3 states that the acceptance is kept in recovery.valuation_ext, read on the ACE side with accepted, accepted_at and accepted_by (DF-EXT-036 to DF-EXT-049). No owner publishes a write operation for either shape: rwb-source-data publishes a data-product read and no write, and the three S1 operations of the Ownership Map are the route decision and the two valuation intake paths. The story therefore records the acceptance in the local decision record, answers the case move to rwb-case and writes no column, and the durable field stays open instead of being invented.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list no table under S1; TSD S1 T3.1 lists valuation as NEW with DF-COL-018 to DF-COL-027, DF-COL-043 stale_flag and DF-COL-044 age_days; the FSD S1 v3 change note and A2.4.3.2 place the acceptance in recovery.valuation_ext with valuation_key, asset_key and valuer_partner_id; the legacy Data table of RWB-E4-004 lists v_ace_valuation, valuation_ext, decision_log_entry, rule_row, recovery_case and assignment and no Workbench-owned table; the routing logic tests accepted_at on the VALUE_ACCEPTED event of R-DIL-12, so the marker must exist somewhere.
area: Data model and ownership, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner and the data steward
proposed: The data owner names the field or the table that holds the accepted value, accepted_at and the accepting user and the owner publishes its write operation. Until then the acceptance is the decision record plus the case move answer, and if the field is a column of rwb_valuation the DB story adds it and this story's writer fills it.

title: The five consumed rows and the case-move answer publish no operation name, and the plan carries no C row for them
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2, T5.1, T5.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.4.2); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP table, R5.7)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3 and 10; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13; CON s3, s12.2, s12.8, s12.9
description: The acceptance reads the appraisal, its outlier flag and its acceptance state from rwb-source-data, reads the case state and answers the case move to rwb-case, reads the rule id, the band policy and the record from rwb-decision, and authorises through rwb-access, and no source publishes an operation name, a parameter or a transport for any of those five rows. TSD S1 T-A.1 lists API-S1-001 only and T5.1 is the row None. The DP table of this legacy key adds no C dependency for DP-03, DP-05, DP-13 and DP-19, so the plan's contract row is empty and the story builds and tests against the documented use, the placeholder and the fakes from Day 1. The outlier flag's field id is not published either, and its element is declared on the data product answer with the placeholder.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack name the three S1 operations and no consumed operation; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists API-S1-001 on /cases/{caseId}/route only and T-A.2 gives RouteRequest and Approval without a field table; TSD S1 T5.1 is the row None and T5.2 lists the calls to P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 without an operation; the FSD S1 A2.4.2 integration points are the row Workbench; the plan rows for RWB-S1-E4004-APP and -CON carry C as an empty list.
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data owner, P3 rwb-case owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: The four owners publish their operation names and the flag's field id before the wave 3 tag; the clients and their fakes are built from the documented use meanwhile, and a published name replaces the placeholder in a minor contract version with no behaviour change.

title: The band the route decision runs on has no published identifiers, boundaries or carrying row, and no S1 rule package is in force
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.4.1, A2.4.3.1 BR-S1-004); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-VAL-04, FEAT-ADM-04); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-38 to R-UNI-40)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 8; s8 BR2, BR6; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data; CON s3, s6, s11, s12.2, s12.6
description: Both legacy criteria require the result to be written with the rule version, and the acceptance exists to fix the band the route decision runs on, but no source defines the band: it names no identifier, no boundary, no list and no row that carries it. The features sheet of the Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the administration of bands, floors and ranges per product to FEAT-ADM-04 of module P4, and the S1 field catalog of FSD S1 A2.4.3.2 does not carry a band field at all. The routing logic carries no S1 rule row for the acceptance and the S1 package is Phase 2, so no rule id exists for the step either. The story therefore reads the band policy in force with its version, records that version with the accepted value, and asserts no boundary, no default and no band name; the contract baseline references the policy as an element of the rule-in-force answer and marks it optional.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.4.1 and FEAT-VAL-04 state that the acceptance fixes the band the route decision runs on and name no band; FSD S1 A2.4.3.1 gives only VR-S1-004-1 and BR-S1-004, that no value a business person may change is written in code and is read from reference data with its version; TSD S1 T3.2 gives LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE and no band list; the Epics 3 to 8 sheet gives FEAT-ADM-04, set the treatment policy by product, as the feature that lets the product head set the bands, floors and ranges; the Rules sheet carries no S1 acceptance row and the S1 package is Phase 2.
area: Rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner and the P4 rwb-access owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The band owner publishes the band list, its boundaries and the row or rule that carries it with its version, or confirms that the band stays a reference-data value administered under FEAT-ADM-04; the record then carries that identifier and version.

title: The element list of RouteRequest and Approval is not published and no source says how the acceptance and the band enter them
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2 API-S1-001); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-004 Endpoints table); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s7 AC2; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13; APP s3, s12.1
description: TSD S1 T-A.2 names the request type RouteRequest and the response type Approval and publishes no field table for either, the legacy story names the operation and no body, and the Ownership Map names no operation that writes an acceptance of its own. The baseline therefore declares the acceptance element set as optional elements of the one published operation, being the valuation key, the accepted value and the appraisal date in the request and the band, the accepted value and the acceptance marker in the answer, and it declares no second operation. No source states whether the acceptance is a required element of a route submission, whether the band is an element of the answer or a value read from the case, or whether a separate write is needed, so the element set cannot be closed without a default.
evidence: TSD S1 T-A.2 gives Purpose, Request RouteRequest, Response Approval, Errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, Authorization and Idempotency, and no field list; the legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E4-004 gives one row, POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/route, with access Treatment and offer U; the ownership rows of the context pack give three S1 operations and none of them is an acceptance write; FSD S1 A2.4.3.2 lists no band field and marks the valuation fields read only.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the solution architect
proposed: The service owner and the architect fix the acceptance element set at the tag as optional elements of API-S1-001, and any separate acceptance write is added later by its owner in a minor version with its rights and its error set.

title: The acceptance fields have two candidate shapes and no source fixes their type, nullability or owner
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.0, T3.1); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.4.3.2, document control change note); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-004 Data table); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s8 BR10; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.7 Tables owned; s13; APP s11
description: The acceptance is carried by accepted, accepted_at, accepted_by, stale_flag and age_days on recovery.valuation_ext in the legacy Data table and in FSD S1 A2.4.3.2, and by accepted, stale_flag and age_days on a NEW valuation table in TSD S1 T3.1 with the DF-COL Field IDs, while the ownership rows give S1 no table and no source publishes the type, the nullability or the format of accepted_at and accepted_by. Because the precedence rule puts the Arch v5 catalogue above the TSD, the baseline declares no table and marks the elements optional, but the element contract cannot be closed for a consumer that needs a required acceptance marker.
evidence: The legacy Data table of RWB-E4-004 lists valuation_ext with valuation_key, accepted, accepted_at, accepted_by, stale_flag, age_days and eight more (DF-EXT-036 to DF-EXT-049); TSD S1 T3.1 declares valuation as NEW with DF-COL-027 accepted, DF-COL-043 stale_flag and DF-COL-044 age_days; TSD S1 T3.0 gives standard record columns only; the FSD S1 v3 change note re-points the valuation field catalog to v_ace_valuation plus recovery.valuation_ext; the ownership rows of the context pack list no table for S1; the routing logic tests accepted_at on R-DIL-12 and gives no type.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner and the data steward
proposed: The data owner confirms one shape and its types before the wave 3 tag; the baseline then declares the element set with that type and nullability in a minor version and retires the other shape with a note in the Change Register.
